canary-server.name: canary-server
canary-server.description: Use this skill when running canary commands through a workspace's command server (canary server start, canary --connect, canary server post/get/wait/cancel).
canary-server.body:
# Canary command server

## What this skill is for

Use this skill when work should run on a specific machine (or be queued) while you submit
and monitor it from elsewhere, or when an agent needs to hand canary commands to a
long-running server and check back later.

## First actions

```console
canary query -c ext.server.overview
canary server status --json        # is a server alive for this workspace? queue?
```

## Start a server (on the machine that does the work, in the workspace)

```console
canary server start                         # blocks and logs to the terminal
canary server start > server.log 2>&1 &     # in the background
nohup canary server start > server.log 2>&1 &   # survives the terminal closing
canary server stop                 # from any machine that sees the workspace
```

Requests run in the server's environment, as it was when the server started (modules,
`PATH`, ...). Nothing from the client's environment is carried: `module load` what the
jobs need *before* `canary server start`.

## Send work

Humans: put `--connect=WHERE` before the command. WHERE is where the workspace search
starts (`.` = the workspace you are in); unlike `-C`, your working directory is kept.

```console
canary --connect=. run -k fast tests        # queues it, prints the request id, returns
canary --connect=/scratch/ws run fast/      # fast/ is relative to where you are
canary server wait ID                       # follow it (the server's terminal shows it too)
canary --connect=. run --only=failed        # reruns and job ids refer to the server's workspace
```

Agents: post the request as data, keep the id, check back (add `--connect=WHERE` before
`server` when outside the workspace tree).

```console
canary server post '{"command": "run", "args": ["--only", "all", "tests"]}'   # -> {"id": "..."}
canary server post request.json    # the same request from a file (- reads stdin)
canary server get ID               # state: queued | running | done | cancelled | failed
canary server wait ID --quiet      # exit code of the command (130 cancelled, 1 failed)
canary server get ID --output      # the command's output
canary server cancel ID
```

The server runs `run`, `exec`, `collect`, `select` and `hpc run`. Read results locally
(`canary status --json`, `canary query ...`); reads never go through the server.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting your own environment (e.g. a module loaded on your desktop) to apply: requests
  run in the server's environment. Set single variables with `"env": {...}` in `post`.

- Expecting requests to run concurrently: they run one at a time, in arrival order.
- Rerunning with `canary run PATH` and getting exit code 7: the default `--only not_pass`
  found nothing to run; pass `--only all`.
- Posting an absolute `cwd` that only exists on your machine: give `cwd` relative to the workspace
  anchor (default `.`), which works even when the server mounts the share elsewhere.
- Running `canary rm` or `canary run -w` while a server runs: refused; stop the server first.
- `canary server start &` without `nohup`: the server stops when the terminal closes.
